newsitem.title: USA: MICRON TECH SHARES SINK ON CHIP PRICE FEARS.
newsitem.headline: MICRON TECH SHARES SINK ON CHIP PRICE FEARS.

text.p: Shares of Micron Technology Inc, which makes memory chips, tumbled about 14 percent on Wednesday as the market worried about falling chip prices, an industry product transition and growing overcapacity.

Both Merrill Lynch and Brown Brothers Harriman downgraded the stock, citing lower 16 megabyte memory chip prices, an industry shift to 64 megabyte chips which would force Micron to play catch-up and a surfeit of memory chips on the market.
Micron shares shed seven points to 43-1/8 on 13.1 million shares after surging to a year high of 58-3/8 last week.

A slump in the 16 megabyte chip prices Micron makes would cut into its profits and margins, analysts said. An oversupply of memory chips and aggressive market penetration by the Taiwanese is adding to price declines, they said.

"There are too many DRAMs being made worldwide relative to demand," said William Milton Jr, an analyst at Brown Brothers Harriman. "The current price which Micron is getting for 16 mb DRAM (dynamic random access memory) chips is about 30 percent lower than the average selling price in the May quarter."

Merrill Lynch analyst Tom Kurlak said he expected the 16 mb (megabyte) DRAM market would hit peak momentum in the fourth quarter, but revenues from it would flatten in the first quarter with a rapid switch to 64 mb memory chips.
Micron's 64 mb chip -- while competitive -- is not in large volume production and Micron is not prepared for an earlier ramp up of it, Kurlak said.
The arrival of Intel Corp's new Pentium II is accelerating the market's shift to 64 mb chips, he said.
But another analyst, Lehman Brothers' Michael Gumport, said it was old news that memory chip prices were falling and market expectations had simply been too high.

"DRAM prices have been slipping steadily throughout this quarter and have actually moved onto a plateau recently," Gumport said. "Consensus estimates had been dramatically above reality. I don't think this reality has changed in two days."
Gumport, who said Micron should have good fourth quarter unit growth, estimated fourth quarter earnings of $0.40 per share.
Merrill's Kurlak cut his quarterly estimate to $0.59 per share from $0.70 and Milton lowered his fourth quarter forecast to $0.42 per share from $0.51 a share.
Kurlak downgraded Micron Technology shares to neutral from accumulate near-term, while Milton went to a short-term avoid rating from a hold rating.
